summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 12, part 42) set at a tea gathering in the Quelton household. Lexy Moran, the viewpoint character, watches Captain Grey, who is moved by finding his sister, and Mrs. Quelton, whom Lexy wonders may be an enemy or may help her with Caroline Enderby. Lexy stays silent while Dr. Quelton serves China tea and Captain Grey talks about Ceylon tea plantations, and she unexpectedly fights back tears before the passage breaks off mid-question.
one_line: Lexy Moran, lost in her own thoughts at a tea party at the Quelton house, is suddenly overcome with tears while Captain Grey talks of his newfound sister.
key_facts: Lexy glances at Captain Grey and is surprised and touched by his grave, pale, almost solemn face as he regards his sister with something like reverence.
Lexy thinks Captain Grey is a poor lonely fellow and hopes his sister is as nice as she looks.
Lexy wonders whether Mrs. Quelton knows about Caroline Enderby and whether she would help Lexy or be her enemy.
The head mistress of Lexy's finishing school often told her: "Alexandra, it is absolutely inexcusable to give way to moods in the company of other people!"
Dr. Quelton is asking his brother-in-law questions about India during the visit.
Mrs. Quelton speaks in a plaintive tone and seems no more desirous to talk than Lexy is.
Dr. Quelton says the tea is China tea that he imports himself and that it has quite a distinctive flavor.
Captain Grey praises the tea, and Lexy finds it very agreeable.
Captain Grey talks behind Lexy about the Ceylon tea plantations in a pathetic voice.
Lexy accepts another cup of tea from Mrs. Quelton, and Dr. Quelton brings it to her.
Lexy's tears well up, and she gulps down her tea hoping it will steady her, but it does not help.
Lexy calls her emotion idiotic and resolves, "I can't be such a chump!"
The passage ends with Lexy turning to Mrs. Quelton and beginning to ask "Are you going to grow any—"
